_README.purpose: Source data for the 10 Edha playtest adversaries (the 6-room test dungeon). foundry-build.js reads this and writes the `edha-adversaries` Actor compendium: one `adversary` actor per entry with embedded `action`/`trait` items. Modelled on the cosmere-rpg companions-and-adversaries pack schema. Source of truth = Edha_Playtest_GM_Cheatsheet.pdf.

actor_fields.role: minion | rival | boss. PDF 'Standard' and 'Elite' both map to 'rival' (the system has only 3 roles).
actor_fields.img: Portrait/sheet image (must exist under Foundry data or core public/icons). Placeholder only once real art exists: the build auto-detects <module>/art/adversaries/<slug>-portrait.(webp|png|jpg) and <slug>-token.* and prefers them (filenames listed per creature in EDHA_ADVERSARY_ART_WISHLIST.md) — drop files + rebuild, no data edit.
actor_fields.token: Token image; defaults to img (or the auto-detected art, see img).
actor_fields.defenses: { phy, cog, spi } — the PDF DEF numbers; written as override+useOverride (DerivedValueField).
actor_fields.deflect: Deflect value (number). Omit for none. Default deflect types = energy/impact/keen (physical armour).
actor_fields.deflectTypes: Optional array overriding which damage types the deflect applies to.
actor_fields.inv: Investiture max (override). DEFAULTS for attuned blocks (ruling 49): any entry with `leylines` gets the PC derivation 2 + max(awa, pre) = 2 (adversary attributes are 0). Set explicitly only to deviate; omit otherwise. 0 if unattuned.
actor_fields.movement: Walk rate in ft (override). Omit/null = system default (25 ft). 0 = immobile.
actor_fields.senses: Senses Range in ft (Character_Building_Rules §Senses Range; Ben 07-16c sight rule). Omit = the AWA table default (adversary AWA 0 → 10 ft). Sets the token's darkness-vision radius (sight.range — lit areas visible beyond it natively) AND the sheet's senses override; the engine's edhaCanSee uses it as the in-darkness sight limit.
actor_fields.conditionImmunities: Array of condition ids the creature is immune to (afflicted/blind/disoriented/exhausted/immobilized/prone/restrained/slowed/stunned/surprised/...). Note: frightened/compelled are Edha-custom and NOT valid system ids.
actor_fields.count: How many appear in the dungeon (informational; the GM drags this many tokens).
actor_fields.folder: Optional Actor-subfolder name, grouped under the 'Edha Adversaries' root folder in the pack (e.g. 'Session 1 — Palewater Ford'). Omit = the legacy 'Playtest Adversaries' folder.
actor_fields.leylines: Array of attuned leyline colors (white/blue/black/red/green). Each gets a default skill rank by role — minion 1 / rival 2 / boss 3 (ruling 40; dice d4/d6/d8, Attunement Range 15/30/60 ft); an explicit `skills` entry overrides the default. Ruling 49: each color ALSO auto-embeds its Leyline Attunement Key (as an action-typed twin) and the actor gets the universal Draw Mana action — attuned adversaries run the same leyline economy as PCs (give them an `inv` pool).
actor_fields.skills: Explicit skill ranks { skillId: rank } — 3-letter core ids (ath/dis/prc/stl/…) or leyline colors. Set each block's 2–3 defensive/contest skills (the §8b lesson: rank 0 means PC opposed tests auto-win).
actor_fields.talents: Array of tree-talent refs embedded as ACTION-TYPED TWINS of the built talent docs: 'Talent Name' or the self-documenting 'Group/Talent Name' (e.g. 'White/Guiding Signal'; unknown/ambiguous ref = hard build error). Twins because the adversary sheet only renders trait/weapon/action sections — a talent-type embed is invisible (07-14 pipe-cleaner). The twin keeps name/img/description/activation/damage/events/effects, so name-based engine automation applies unchanged, and ownership gates go through the flag-aware edhaIsTalent (flags.edha-content.adversaryTalent). No prereqs. Ruling 40: HUMANS use talents as written (this field); ANIMALS/MONSTERS get adaptations authored as bespoke items instead. Talent costs are the talent's own — usually Investiture, so give the actor an `inv` pool.

item_fields.kind: action | trait | weapon. Default action. Passives = trait. weapon = a REAL weapon-type item (renders in the sheet's weapon section, lootable): same attack/damage/range fields, roll stays the action-shaped skill_test + flat modifierFormula so PDF numbers hold at any skill rank. ⚑⚑ PIPE-CLEANER until the schema dump verifies the weapon DataModel (2026-07-15) — fleet migration of the remaining attack items is backlogged on that.
item_fields.weaponId: Optional, kind=weapon only: the system weapon-registry id (e.g. 'shortsword'). Written to both system.type and system.weaponId (one sticks, the other strips — dump decides which is real).
item_fields.name: Item name.
item_fields.cost: Passive | 1 Action | 2 Actions | 3 Actions | Free Action | Reaction | Special. Default '1 Action' for actions, 'Passive' for traits.
item_fields.consume: Resource cost string, parsed like talents: 'N Focus' / 'N Investiture', comma-separated. Omit for none.
item_fields.attack: Flat attack bonus (number). Present => the item becomes a rollable skill_test (d20 + this bonus via modifierFormula). With `damage` the play button rolls attack + damage; WITHOUT `damage` it is a to-hit-only attack (grab/grapple) — put the on-hit effect in `rider`.
item_fields.range: Stat-line range text, e.g. 'Reach 5 ft.', 'Range 60 ft.', 'melee'. Also infers melee(hwp)/ranged(lwp) skill if `skill` not given.
item_fields.damage: Damage formula, e.g. '1d6+2'. With `attack` => weapon strike; without `attack` => damage-only roll (heals/AoE, raw dice).
item_fields.damageType: energy | impact | keen | spirit | vital | heal.
item_fields.graze: Optional graze-override formula. Default = the damage dice with flat mods stripped (system default).
item_fields.skill: Optional skill id override for the test (cosmetic; attributes are 0 so the flat `attack` carries the bonus).
item_fields.uses: Optional limited-uses note appended to the text (e.g. '1/round', '1/scene'). Informational.
item_fields.rider: Extra hit-clause text appended after the Hit line (HTML allowed).
item_fields.text: Full rules text for traits / utility actions with no attack. HTML allowed; supports [[damage NdM Type]] and [[test skill=xxx dc=N]] enrichers.
item_fields.events: OPTIONAL array of native event rules — [{event, handler, description?}] — the SAME edha-* vocabulary as PC talents (the build mints the 16-char rule ids; never author ids or the map form). THE WIRING STANDARD (Ben 2026-07-16): every ability whose text names a trigger MUST carry either native automation (attack/damage/heal fields), an events rule (edha-gm-cue at minimum), or an explicit 'GM-run — NO NAMEABLE HOOK: <reason>' line in its text. A bare 'GM-run' label is a lint-able smell, not an answer.

_README.buckets: RETIRED 2026-07-16 (the old text deferred triggered abilities to a future 'Phase-3 trigger model' — that model exists now). Every ability ships as a real item; strikes/heals are rollable; triggered/threshold abilities carry `events` rules (see item_fields.events). The only hand-run abilities are the ones with a written no-nameable-hook rationale (Combat Training, Pack Tactics, Veil).

Trooper.biography:
Rank-and-file soldiers. They appear in groups; the dungeon fields five.

(Foc 2 added so Brace can pay its cost — the cheatsheet omits a Focus pool.)

items.name: Brace
items.text: Until the start of the Trooper's next turn, attacks against it are made with 1 disadvantage.

events.description: On use: the Trooper gains the Braced marker (attackers roll at disadvantage), auto-expiring.

The Living Lock.biography: A warded mechanism that guards a sealed door. It cannot move (walk rate 0). Spiritual defense (10) is an estimate — not printed on the cheatsheet.

items.name: Glyph Pulse
items.text:
Every 2 rounds (at the end of the Living Lock's turn on even rounds), each creature touching or adjacent to the Lock takes [[damage 1d6 Spirit]] damage, resolved against Cognitive defense (a mental glyph).

The engine cues the GM at the end of the Lock's turn on even rounds; the GM rolls and applies (who counts as 'touching' is a table read).

handler.note: Glyph Pulse: each creature touching or adjacent to the Lock takes 1d6 Spirit, resolved against Cognitive defense.

events.description: GM cue at the end of the Lock's turn, even rounds.

Stonebound Captain.biography: An elite frontline commander encased in living stone.

items.name: Devastating Blow
items.rider: If the hit exceeds the target's Physical defense by 5 or more, the target is knocked Prone.

handler.note: Devastating Blow landed — if the attack total exceeded the target's Physical defense by 5+, it is knocked Prone.

events.description: GM cue on Devastating Blow's own hit (the margin read stays with the GM).

items.name: Reactive Strike
items.rider: Triggered when an adjacent enemy takes an action.

handler.note: Reaction, 1 Focus — Reactive Strike is live: if this enemy takes an action in reach, the Captain may strike it.

events.description: GM cue once when an enemy starts its turn in reach (per-action cues would spam).

items.name: Brace
items.text: Until the start of the Captain's next turn, attacks against it are made with 2 disadvantage.

events.description: On use: the Captain gains the Braced marker (attackers roll at 2 disadvantage — the item text carries the count), auto-expiring.

items.name: Combat Training
items.text:
Once per round, the Captain can turn one of its own misses into a graze automatically (a free graze).

Ruled miss→graze (Ben 2026-07-16 — the source PDF sentence was garbled). GM-run — NO NAMEABLE HOOK: the miss/graze/hit adjudication happens in the GM's application step and is never module-visible data.

Wrenchmaster.biography: A probability-manipulating saboteur who bends luck for their allies and against their foes.

items.name: Probability Net
items.text: One creature the Wrenchmaster can sense suffers −1d6 to their next test before the end of their next turn.

events.description: On use with a target: their next test takes −1d6 (auto-injected, labeled on the roll). Engine drift note: the mod rides until their next test rather than lapsing at end of next turn.

items.name: Tactical Insight
items.text: One ally rerolls a test they just made and keeps the new result.

items.name: Plot Die Swap
items.text: Choose the face of one ally's plot die, setting it to a result of the Wrenchmaster's choice.

items.name: Calc Strike
items.text: One ally gains +3 to one test they make this round.

Cinderhound.biography: Fire-wreathed pack hunters. The dungeon fields three.

items.name: Bite
items.rider: The target sheds light (as a torch) until the end of its next turn.

events.description: Bitten creatures shed a 20-ft flame light (the Kindle light rider, auto-applied on damage).

items.name: Cinder Coat
items.text:
When a creature hits the Cinderhound with a melee attack, that attacker takes [[damage 1d4 Energy]] splash damage.

Auto-applied by the engine (adjacent attackers only), chain-guarded.

events.description: Melee splash-back: adjacent attackers take 1d4 Energy automatically when they damage the hound.

items.name: Pack Tactics
items.text:
The Cinderhound attacks with an advantage while at least one other Cinderhound is also targeting the same creature.

Engine-run via the aggro ledger (Ben 07-16c): each hound token remembers its last attack target; attacking a creature another living hound last attacked rolls with advantage automatically (whispered card states which packmate). 'Targeting' ≈ last-attacked — the GM's own memory of intent still overrules.

events.description: Advantage when a living packmate's aggro is on the same creature.

Frostbinder.biography: An ice-and-fate adept who freezes foes and rewrites the odds.

items.name: Frost Lance
items.rider: On a hit, the target is Slowed until the end of its next turn.

events.description: On Frost Lance's own hit: the victim is Slowed, timed to expire at the end of ITS next turn.

items.name: Glimpse the Path
items.text: Until the end of the Frostbinder's next turn, it makes all of its rolls with an advantage.

items.name: Anchor of Probability
items.text: Force one creature within 30 feet to reroll a test; the GM chooses which result is used.

items.name: Predictive Ward
items.text: All attacks against the Frostbinder are made with 1 disadvantage.

Stalker.biography:
Concealed crossbow skirmishers. The dungeon fields two.

(Inv 2 added so Fade can pay its cost — the cheatsheet omits an Investiture pool.)

items.name: Fade
items.text: Triggered when an attack against the Stalker grazes or misses: the Stalker gains Concealment until the end of its next turn.

handler.note: Reaction, 1 Investiture — if that was a GRAZE, Fade: Concealment until the end of its next turn (toggle the Fade marker). On a clean MISS nothing fires here — no damage is ever applied, so cue yourself.

events.description: GM cue on damage (covers the graze half of the trigger; a true miss applies no damage and has no hook).

items.name: Veil
items.text:
While in cover or low light, the Stalker is Concealed. Noticing or attacking it requires a [[test skill=prc dc=15]].

The LIGHT half is engine-run (Ben 07-16c: lighting is data): the Veil marker auto-enables while the token stands unlit and auto-releases when lit. The COVER half stays a table read — toggle the marker by hand for cover; the engine never fights a manual toggle.

events.description: Auto-toggles the Veil marker on the illumination test (cover stays GM-toggled).

Stitchmother.biography: The dungeon boss — a flesh-weaving aberration that knits its thralls and itself back together. Phase 2 triggers once, the first time it drops below 70 HP (see the Phase 2 trait). Run Phase 2 by hand: raise max HP by 20 and heal to 90, +1 Strength / +1 Speed, attacks deal +2 Vital, Suture Cradle ends, it auto-regenerates [[damage 2d6 Heal]] at the start of each of its turns (no cost), and it may make a free Scalpel-Strike whenever it heals a creature adjacent to its target.

items.name: Scalpel-Strike
items.rider: Deals +4 damage against a creature marked by Vital Diagram.

events.description: +4 (labeled on the roll) when the current target carries the Vital Diagram mark. The Deflect bypass stays GM-applied — riders can't reach the deflect math.

items.name: Suture Cradle
items.rider: Sustained (1 Investiture at the start of each of the Stitchmother's turns). When the healed target is hit, the Stitchmother must succeed on a Discipline test (DC 10 + damage taken) to keep the cradle active — TARGET the creature when using this; the engine tracks the cradle and auto-rolls the Discipline test on every hit it takes (keep or the cradle ends).

items.name: Vital Diagram
items.text:
Mark one PC the Stitchmother can sense. Until the end of the scene, all hits against the marked creature deal +4 Vital damage and bypass that creature's Deflect.

Target the PC and use: the Vital Diagram mark (token icon) is applied by the engine; Scalpel-Strike's +4 keys on it automatically. Scene-long — clear the mark by hand at scene end. The Deflect bypass stays GM-applied.

events.description: On use with a target: applies the Vital Diagram mark (scene-long, GM-cleared).

items.name: Adaptive Mutation
items.text:
Grant a Mutated Thrall either Bone Spurs (its Slam gains +2 Keen) or Venom Glands (its Slam inflicts Afflicted, 2 Vital/turn). By round 3 the Stitchmother can have stacked both onto a single thrall.

After using: toggle the granted upgrade's marker on that Thrall's sheet (both are baked, disabled by default) — the markers make the grant visible; the Slam bonuses stay GM-applied.

items.name: Reknit Form
items.text: The Stitchmother removes one Injury from itself or an adjacent ally.

items.name: Phase 2
items.text:
Trigger (once, the first time the Stitchmother drops below 70 HP): its maximum HP increases by 20 and it heals to 90; it gains +1 Strength and +1 Speed; its attacks deal +2 Vital; Suture Cradle ends; it auto-regenerates [[damage 2d6 Heal]] at the start of each of its turns at no cost; and it may make a free Scalpel-Strike whenever it heals a creature adjacent to its target.

The engine cues the GM at the crossing; the transformation itself is GM-run (sheet edits).

handler.note: PHASE 2 (once): max HP +20 and heal to 90; +1 Strength, +1 Speed; attacks +2 Vital; Suture Cradle ends; 2d6 auto-regen at turn start (free); free Scalpel-Strike whenever she heals a creature adjacent to her target.

events.description: GM cue the first time she crosses 70 HP.

Mutated Thrall.biography: The Stitchmother's reworked servants. The dungeon fields two.

items.name: Mutation Upgrade
items.text:
If the Stitchmother grants this thrall Bone Spurs, its Slam gains +2 Keen damage. If granted Venom Glands, its Slam inflicts Afflicted (2 Vital/turn) on a hit. By round 3 both upgrades can be active at once.

GM-run — NO NAMEABLE HOOK today: the grant lives as a toggled marker AE, and conditional-on-marker damage riders aren't a primitive yet (first consumer wanted: a whenSelfEffect rider condition). Toggle the marker; apply the Slam bonus by hand.

Corvaine Raider.biography:
Corvaine border regulars raiding under Sgt. Roek — soldiers, not bandits (EDHA_SESSION_1_SCRIPT.md §2). Unpaid and starving, but equipped with suspiciously new, matched, Malcurr-stamped gear — the un-missable clue: searching a downed Raider puts a stamped blade in a PC's hand.

Scaling: ±1 Raider per PC over/under 3; squishy party → deflect 1 / HP 10.

items.name: Break
items.text: When the Raider is first reduced below half HP, or when an ally drops, it may immediately Disengage and flee. These are not fanatics.

handler.note: Reaction — below half HP: the Raider may immediately Disengage and flee. These are not fanatics.

events.description: GM cue at half HP.

handler.note: Reaction — an ally dropped: the Raider may immediately Disengage and flee.

events.description: GM cue when an ally drops.

Corvaine Line-Caller.biography: White-attuned Corvaine ground-stock (ruling 36) — the one invested minion in the raid (ruling 39's 1-in-8, a force-multiplier). Runs its White tree talents as written (ruling 40): Guiding Signal (1 Action, 1 Investiture — designate a character within Attunement Range 15 ft; the engine card grants the Plot Die to an ally who tests against them this round) and Ordered Advance (2 Actions, 1 Investiture — this round, when it moves, allies within 10 ft move half Speed without provoking). This is why the wade looks drilled and the whole line seems to turn its head at once.

items.name: Break
items.text: When the Line-Caller is first reduced below half HP, or when an ally drops, it may immediately Disengage and flee. These are not fanatics.

handler.note: Reaction — below half HP: the Line-Caller may immediately Disengage and flee. These are not fanatics.

events.description: GM cue at half HP.

handler.note: Reaction — an ally dropped: the Line-Caller may immediately Disengage and flee.

events.description: GM cue when an ally drops.

items.name: The Line Falls Apart
items.text:
GM-run: when the Line-Caller drops or flees, the volleys stop — Raiders act individually, and Break triggers one round earlier.

(The lesson ruling 39 teaches: invested minions are force-multipliers — shoot the signaler.)

handler.note: The Line-Caller is down — the volleys stop: Raiders act individually and Break triggers one round earlier. (Fleeing triggers this too — GM-called.)

events.description: GM cue when the Line-Caller drops.

Sergeant Halden Roek.biography:
Corvaine regular leading the raid — hollow-cheeked under too-good armor; ashamed and doing it anyway (EDHA_SESSION_1_SCRIPT.md §2). He wants food for his own starving unit and would rather not kill.

Talk-outs: Persuasion/Leadership vs. his Spiritual defense (DC 13) — offer a split, or point out Withervale starves too → he takes one barge's load and goes. Intimidation (DC 14) → he calls the break a round sooner. Feeding/healing his people is remembered — a contact inside Corvaine's border troops for later acts.

items.name: Press the Line
items.rider: On a hit, one allied Raider may immediately make a crossbow shot as a Reaction.

handler.note: One allied Raider may immediately make a crossbow shot as a Reaction.

events.description: GM cue on Press the Line's own hit.

items.name: Cover Their Retreat
items.text: When an ally within 20 ft would drop, Roek grants it disadvantage-to-be-hit until his next turn instead (shoves them behind cover).

handler.note: Reaction, 1 Focus — Roek may shove them behind cover instead: the drop is prevented and they have disadvantage-to-be-hit until his next turn (GM: roll the drop back if he reacts).

events.description: GM cue when an ally within 20 ft drops.

items.name: White-Attuned
items.text: Ruling 39: rival tier is always invested (one leyline). Roek is Corvaine ground-stock like his line-caller, and his coordination is talent as much as drill — Press the Line and Cover Their Retreat are White tree-kin (Guiding Signal / Unbreakable Line), run natural: ruling 40's 'unless otherwise noted' case. He'd tell you it's just soldiering. On the Corvaine plains, the two have never been different things.

items.name: Not a Bandit
items.text: GM-run: Roek accepts a surrender or a fair split and stops. Reduced below 1/3 HP, he calls the break himself: 'Enough. We're done. Take your grain.'

handler.note: Below 1/3 HP — Roek calls the break himself: 'Enough. We're done. Take your grain.' (He also stops for any surrender or fair split.)

events.description: GM morale cue at 1/3 HP.

Mistheron.biography:
Man-tall Blue-attuned wading birds (canon §5c; bargefolk river-cant) — starving because the river's fish are wasting-stuck. They come for food, not war: the barge dog, a grain sack, a lone poleman at the rail. Ribs under feathers; afraid of the light. First worked example of ruling 40's beast adaptation (EDHA_SESSION_1_SCRIPT.md §3b).

Scaling: 2 birds baseline (3 PCs); 4+ PCs → 3 birds; injured party → 1. This beat bruises — it never threatens the boat. Deflect 1 = dense fog-gray plumage.

items.name: The Seeming
items.text:
The Blue tree talent Phantom Double, adapted per ruling 40 (beasts run tree abilities as natural adaptations): self-only, at will.

Its image stands a pace from its body. Using this places the seeming beside the bird (1 health — any hit breaks it). Every enemy who can see it tests Perception against its Cognitive defense (engine-rolled): on a failure only the seeming is real to them; on a success it is empty air. When the seeming breaks, the bird stands plainly seen. Its call sounds from the seeming, never the body.

items.name: Spearing Beak
items.rider: +1d6 against a character who is taken in by the seeming.

events.description: +1d6 (flavor-labeled on the roll) when the current target is taken in by The Seeming.

items.name: Snatch and Wade
items.targets: one Small-or-smaller creature or a carried/loose object
items.rider: It grips instead of dealing damage and immediately moves its full Speed into the fog. (This is what it actually wants.)

items.name: Fade
items.text: When its seeming breaks or it takes damage, it moves 10 ft without provoking, into fog if possible — once unseen it may raise The Seeming again.

handler.note: Reaction, 1 Focus — the bird may move 10 ft without provoking, into fog if possible; once unseen it may raise The Seeming again.

events.description: GM cue when the Mistheron takes damage.

handler.note: Reaction, 1 Focus — its seeming broke; it may move 10 ft without provoking, into fog if possible, then raise The Seeming again once unseen.

events.description: GM cue when its seeming breaks.

items.name: Starving, Not Fanatic
items.text: GM-run: bloodied (≤ half HP), or if its partner is bloodied, it breaks off into the fog and does not return. Thrust fire at it or raise a sustained din (the barge bell) and it fades within a round.

handler.note: Bloodied — it breaks off into the fog and does not return (its partner breaks too if also bloodied).

events.description: GM morale cue at half HP.

Drownlight Colony.biography:
Pair-attuned Black/Blue lure-hunters of the Lunavar fens (canon §5c, ruling 69) — colony of cold small bodies, seen only as the light. It has no attack: the encounter is about trust and terrain — the danger is deep water, mireground, or the stillback the light leads to. Sad, not evil: starving colonies luring bolder.

Scaling: one colony per party — more lights, not more colonies. Per-block leyline override (ruling 69): pair-attunement carries two colors at minion rank.

items.name: The False Lantern
items.text: The colony places its lure-light at a point it can sense within 60 ft. Every enemy who can see the light tests Perception against the colony's Cognitive defense (engine-rolled, the Seeming pattern): on a failure the light reads as whatever lamp, torch, or pool-gleam they would hope to see there — GM-run, it drifts a pace off the safe path each round toward deep water, mireground, or a waiting hunter. On a success it is marshfire, plainly.

items.name: The Mark
items.text: The colony always knows which creature within 60 ft is nearest its end — most injured, sickest, most exhausted — and lures that one first (the Black half of the pair).

items.name: Gutter and Re-light
items.text: On taking any damage, the lights wink out and re-light 30 ft away.

handler.note: Reaction — the lights gutter and re-light 30 ft away.

events.description: GM cue when the colony takes damage.

items.name: Only Lights
items.text: GM-run: bloodied (≤ half HP), the colony scatters into the reeds and does not re-form this scene — steel disperses it instantly (ruling 34: never tougher).

handler.note: Bloodied — the colony scatters and does not re-form this scene.

events.description: GM morale cue at half HP.

Reedling.biography:
Runner-tangles of a fen-heart (canon §5c, ruling 69) — the marsh cousins of Thalendor's rootlings (ruling 32). Deflect 1 = woven reed. Displaced by the Westward line's drain, they mine paddies and rice-caches for the Green in them; near a gone-to-weir heart they screen and delay. They defend, they do not pursue.

Scaling: 2–3 swarms screening the fen-heart, or 1–2 harassing a causeway crossing.

items.name: Whip-Lash
items.rider: A struck target that is in water, or Small-or-smaller, is dragged 5 ft.

items.name: Weir-Work
items.text: The swarm weaves a knee-high barrier across a 10-ft edge: difficult terrain; DC 12 Athletics to cross at speed; a poled boat is stopped until the weir is breached or lifted over.

items.name: Runners, Not Soldiers
items.text: GM-run: bloodied (≤ half HP), the swarm scatters into the reeds.

handler.note: Bloodied — the reedlings scatter into the reeds.

events.description: GM morale cue at half HP.

Gone-to-Weir Fen-Heart.biography:
A blight-mad fen-heart (canon §5c, ruling 69) — 'gone to weir': locked in un-clearing disease, instincts misfiring, damming and drowning everything in its water. Deflect 2 = sodden wood. Wrong, not evil — and never tougher for being sick (ruling 34): steel and fire work. The out: it attacks what MOVES in its water — root-warden-style craft (stillness, offerings, cut-signs, patience — ruling 32) can end this without a kill. At 0 HP it does not die — too blighted to finish (§1a): it goes still, the weirs stand, and clearing them is labor. The victory is sad on purpose.

Schema: size 'large' + creatureType 'custom' (the repo enum has no huge/plant) — it PLAYS huge: set the token to 3x3 or 4x4 on placement. Scaling: cap Call the Runners at 1 swarm for 3 PCs.

items.name: Dragging Roots
items.rider: The struck target is pulled 10 ft toward the heart, or into open water.

items.name: Throw the Weir
items.text: A woven wall rises across a 20-ft line anywhere in its water: blocks movement, DC 14 Athletics to breach; boats are stopped dead.

items.name: Drown the Field
items.text: Once per scene. It opens its weirs — a 30-ft-radius zone floods to deep water and difficult terrain for the rest of the scene.

items.name: Call the Runners
items.text: 1d4 Reedling swarms surface where the GM places them (the scaling knob — cap for small parties).

items.name: Wrong, Not Evil
items.text: It attacks what moves in its water. A character who goes still and silent for a full round is ignored; warden-craft (offerings, cut-signs, patience) can calm the fight closed — reward the attempt.

items.name: The Madness Slackens
items.text: GM-run: bloodied (≤ half HP), it stops targeting downed characters. At 0 HP it goes still instead of dying — the blight stands.

handler.note: Bloodied — the madness slackens: it stops targeting downed characters.

events.description: GM cue at half HP.

handler.note: It goes still — not dead (too blighted to finish, §1a). The weirs stand; what remains is labor, not violence.

events.description: GM cue near 0 HP.

Stillback.biography:
The fens' apex ambusher (canon §5c, ruling 69) — a crocodilian the length of a barge whose stillness is a seeming (the mistheron's Seeming turned inward; ruling 38's one magic). Deflect 2 = armored hide. Swim 40 ft. Starving because the honest catch is gone (predator's fork, ruling 34) — it takes stock and causeway travelers now, and every attack is sad, not evil. Pairs naturally with a Drownlight Colony as lure and anvil.

Scaling: one is a rival-tier set piece; add the colony, not a second stillback.

items.name: The Causeway Seeming
items.text:
Blue adaptation (ruling 40): the Seeming worn as stillness — always on until it moves.

Until it first moves each scene, anyone who would notice it tests Perception against its Cognitive defense (engine-rolled): on a failure it reads as terrain — a mudbank, a log, causeway stone. Its first attack from unbroken stillness is made from ambush.

handler.note: Ambush Bite's +1d6 rider applies vs the fooled.

events.description: Engine-rolled belief test on its first attack against each target per scene — the strike from stillness (ambush-belief ledger; whenTargetFooled riders read it).

items.name: Ambush Bite
items.rider: +1d6 against a character who is taken in by the seeming.

events.description: +1d6 (flavor-labeled on the roll) when the current target is taken in by The Causeway Seeming.

items.name: Seize and Roll
items.rider: On a hit it grips and drags the target 10 ft toward deep water (DC 14 Athletics to break the grip). While gripping, it may roll: the gripped target takes 1d8 impact. NO NAMEABLE HOOK: to-hit-only grab — a hit that deals no damage makes no document write, so there is no engine hook; the GM rolls the attack and adjudicates the grip.

items.name: Slide Under
items.text: On taking damage while within reach of deep water: it submerges and moves 15 ft unseen.

handler.note: Reaction, 1 Focus — it submerges and moves 15 ft unseen (deep water required).

events.description: GM cue when the Stillback takes damage.

items.name: Patient, Not Cruel
items.text: GM-run: bloodied (≤ half HP), it releases whatever it holds and slides under, gone for good.

handler.note: Bloodied — it releases its grip and slides under; it does not return.

events.description: GM morale cue at half HP.

Wasting-Eater Stillback.biography: A stillback that chose the other fork (ruling 34): it ate the stuck-wasting shoals, and the murrain has it — months sick, ribs under armor, still hunting because it cannot stop and cannot die of what it has. Weaker than a sound one; worse to find. Its seeming frays (tests to see through it have advantage) and it no longer retreats. No combat transmission — ruling 34's channel is eating: butchering or eating this animal passes the wasting (slow, GM-paced consequence — note it if the party field-dresses the kill).

items.name: The Frayed Seeming
items.text: As The Causeway Seeming, but the stillness is imperfect — tests to see through it are made with advantage.

handler.note: Sick Bite's +1d6 rider applies vs the fooled.

events.description: As the Causeway Seeming, but the target's Perception rolls with advantage (frayed).

items.name: Sick Bite
items.rider: +1d6 against a character who is taken in by the seeming.

events.description: +1d6 when the current target is taken in by The Frayed Seeming.

items.name: Cannot Stop
items.text: GM-run: it does not retreat and does not release — bloodied changes nothing (the wasting hunts through it). Steel works as it always does (ruling 34: never tougher); this fight ends one way, and it is a mercy. NO NAMEABLE HOOK: morale that never changes has nothing to cue.

Noonwing.biography:
Lunavar's diurnal apex (canon §5c, ruling 70) — the White thermal-soaring raptor that made the nation nocturnal. Deflect 1 = dense feathers. Fly 80 (soar) / walk 10. It hunts WORKED PATTERN by daylight and cannot soar at night or under rain/fog — the night calendar is the counterplay a whole culture built. A healthy predator, not a wrongness: the famine arc is thinner margins, not sickness.

Scaling: ONE noonwing is the encounter — the real fight is the party's choice between speed (rhythm, seen) and safety (broken, half speed) on open fen. It bruises escort pacing more than HP bars.

items.name: The Patterned Eye
items.text:
White adaptation (ruling 40): pattern-sense, always on while aloft in daylight.

From altitude it perceives worked pattern — groups moving in rhythm, work lines, marching columns, rowed wakes — across its whole line of sight in open fen. GM-run: a group traveling broken (scattered, out of step, at half speed) is not read as prey; fog, rain, and full cover defeat the eye entirely.

items.name: Thermal Rider
items.text: While aloft in daylight it climbs without cost and cannot be reached by melee. It cannot soar at night or in rain/fog. After The Stoop it is at ground level until the end of its next turn — that window is the fight.

items.name: The Stoop
items.rider: Only from aloft. The struck target is knocked prone. Instead of dealing damage it may snatch a Small-or-smaller creature or carried object and take it into the climb-out. After the stoop it is grounded until the end of its next turn.

handler.note: Stoop hit — target prone (or snatched, if Small-or-smaller and the noonwing chose to grab instead of wound). The noonwing is GROUNDED until the end of its next turn.

events.description: GM cue when The Stoop deals damage.

items.name: Wingstorm
items.rider: Each creature in the burst is pushed 5 ft; the noonwing may take off after the buffet.

items.name: Wings Up, Wings Gone
items.text: GM-run: bloodied (≤ half HP), it climbs away and does not return — a healthy predator with no reason to die today. It also disengages on its own at dusk or as weather closes.

handler.note: Bloodied — it climbs away and does not return.

events.description: GM morale cue at half HP.

Wrongwake.biography:
The cold lakes' apex ambusher (canon §5c, ruling 80) — a pike the length of a skiff, pale as lakebed stone, whose every sound arrives from somewhere else (the mistheron's Seeming moved to the sound channel; ruling 38's one magic). Deflect 1 = heavy scale. Swim 50 ft / flounder 10 on land. Starving bold (predator's fork, ruling 34): dogs off jetties, a hand off a gunwale, the ferry lanes — sad, not evil. Winter: it hunts under new ice, and half the ice-road wisdom children think is about thickness is about listening wrong.

Scaling: one wrongwake IS the encounter — dress the scene with hushwing quiet and lamplight, don't add a second fish.

items.name: The Thrown Voice
items.text:
Blue adaptation (ruling 40): the Seeming moved to the sound channel — always on.

Every sound it makes arrives from a point it chooses within 30 ft of its body. While it is submerged and unseen, hearing-based attempts to locate it fail outright; a character targeted by its first attack each scene tests Perception against its Cognitive defense (engine-rolled) — on a failure the attack comes from ambush.

handler.note: Breach Strike's +1d6 rider applies vs the fooled.

events.description: Engine-rolled belief test on its first attack against each target per scene (ambush-belief ledger; whenTargetFooled riders read it).

items.name: Breach Strike
items.rider: +1d6 against a character taken in by the Thrown Voice.

events.description: +1d6 (flavor-labeled on the roll) when the current target is taken in by The Thrown Voice.

items.name: Drag Under
items.rider: On a hit it grips and pulls the target 10 ft toward deep water (DC 13 Athletics to break). A target pulled under is submerged — no air, no speech. NO NAMEABLE HOOK: to-hit-only grab — a hit that deals no damage makes no document write, so there is no engine hook; the GM rolls the attack and adjudicates the grip.

items.name: Slip the Sound
items.text: When an attack misses it: it shifts 10 ft submerged — the next attempt to find it starts from the wrong splash. NO NAMEABLE HOOK: a missed attack leaves no document write — no Foundry hook exists for “an attack missed you”; the GM narrates the reaction (1 Focus).

items.name: Cold, Not Cruel
items.text: GM-run: bloodied (≤ half HP), it releases everything, sounds once from three places at once, and is gone deep.

Wasting-Eater Wrongwake.biography: A wrongwake that chose the other fork (ruling 34): it ate the stuck-wasting shoals, and the murrain has it — ribs under scale, months sick, still hunting because it cannot stop and cannot die of what it has. Weaker, never tougher — steel works, and the fight is a mercy. It keeps the Thrown Voice (attunement is lineage) but it is too sick to be quick.

items.name: The Thrown Voice
items.text:
As the sound wrongwake — attunement is lineage, sickness doesn't silence it.

Every sound it makes arrives from a point it chooses within 30 ft of its body. While submerged and unseen, hearing-based location fails; a character targeted by its first attack each scene tests Perception against its Cognitive defense (engine-rolled) — failure means ambush.

handler.note: Sick Breach's +1d6 rider applies vs the fooled.

events.description: Engine-rolled belief test on its first attack against each target per scene (ambush-belief ledger; whenTargetFooled riders read it).

items.name: Sick Breach
items.rider: +1d6 against a character taken in by the Thrown Voice.

events.description: +1d6 when the current target is taken in by The Thrown Voice.

items.name: The Passed Wasting
items.text: Ruling 34: its flesh carries the wasting — anything that eats of it buys the slow, GM-paced consequence. Field-dressing this catch is the mistake. NO NAMEABLE HOOK: downtime consequence, GM-run.

items.name: It Cannot Stop
items.text: GM-run: it never disengages and fights past bloodied — not brave, just unable to end.

Wake-Eel Shoal.biography:
The Attendant (canon §5c, ruling 80) — a colony of blind, arm-long Black lake-eels that perceive what leaves a body. Swim 30. For generations they rose in a ring around a completing death and dispersed; post-seal the deaths don't finish, so the colonies gather permanent under the gone-cold islands (ruling 74). The Lamp-tenders read them like an instrument.

Scaling: scene pressure for ferry and swimming beats, not a standalone fight. One shoal; thicken the dread, not the HP.

items.name: The Attendance
items.text:
Black adaptation (ruling 40): the death-sense, colony-wide.

The shoal always knows the most badly hurt creature within 60 ft and drifts toward the failing. When a creature within 60 ft dies, the shoal rises in a slow ring on the surface — visible from shore.

handler.note: The Attendance — the shoal drifts toward the most badly hurt creature within 60 ft; on any death within 60 ft it rises in a surface ring visible from shore.

events.description: GM cue (enemy-turn-start).

items.name: Worry the Failing
items.range: Reach 5 ft. (targets in the water only)
items.rider: Against a bloodied target: +1d4, and the target tests Athletics (DC 12) — on a failure the shoal drags it under the surface until the start of its next turn (no breath, no speech; ranged attacks and sight from above the water are fouled; surfacing costs half its movement).

handler.note: Worry the Failing hit — if the target is bloodied: +1d4, and Athletics DC 12 or dragged under until the start of its next turn (no breath/speech, above-water attacks and sight fouled, surfacing costs half movement).

events.description: GM cue when Worry the Failing deals damage.

items.name: A Thousand Small Bodies
items.text: Single-target Strikes deal half damage to the shoal; any area effect scatters it — it reforms at the start of its next turn unless the water is left. NO NAMEABLE HOOK: halving/scatter is GM-applied on the fly (swarm bookkeeping, no engine surface).

items.name: Attendance, Not Appetite
items.text: GM-run: it never pursues onto land. It wants the dying attended, not the living eaten — leaving the water ends the encounter.

Fellstag.biography:
The Walking Thicket (canon §5c, ruling 80) — a great upland stag of the peat moors, antlers and spine carrying living growth, Green-attuned through the stored centuries of the peat. Deflect 1 = thorn-hide. The fight is a maze being built around the party while something with a spread of thorned antler decides which corridor you die in. It defends ground; it does not hunt.

Scaling: the maze is the encounter — run the ground honestly and 30 HP is terrifying. Blight-gray variant (ruling 34, weaker): HP 22, loses The Waking Ground and Sudden Wall (nothing grows — the growth is locked), fights inside its existing gray maze, and never leaves.

items.name: The Waking Ground
items.text:
Green adaptation (ruling 40): Green Leyline Attunement's terrain-on-draw, grown as thicket.

When it Draws Mana, a patch of thicket (difficult terrain, ~10-ft square) rises within Attunement Range — click-to-place.

ENGINE-NATIVE VIA Draw Mana: its embedded Green Key click-places the square on each draw; Thorn Hedge keen rides engine-placed patches automatically.

items.name: Thorn Hedge
items.text:
Thorn Field, adapted — the engine treats Thorn Hedge as Thorn Field ownership.

Its thickets deal ½[Tier][Die] keen (floor(1d6/2) at its tier and rank) to any character entering or starting their turn inside them. Engine-placed patches (Draw Mana / Sudden Wall) deal it automatically via the region hazard; the GM applies the same roll for the pre-existing maze.

handler.note: Thorn Hedge — floor(1d6/2) keen to any character entering or starting a turn in HAND-PLACED maze thicket (engine-placed patches auto-deal via the region hazard).

events.description: GM cue each hostile turn start (hand-placed maze thicket only — engine regions self-run).

items.name: Sudden Wall
items.text:
Sudden Growth, adapted.

A thicket patch rises adjacent to any character it can sense — sealing a corridor, cutting a retreat.

events.description: Sudden Growth's engine path: click-to-place a [Size] difficult-terrain Region within Attunement Range (Thorn Hedge keen rides it).

items.name: Herding Antlers
items.text:
Drive the Prey, adapted — the engine runs Herding Antlers on Drive the Prey's contest path.

Test Green vs. Survival against a character within 30 ft (engine-rolled: target it and use again): on a success the target is Slowed and must move away from the fellstag on its next turn — and the maze decides where away leads. Thorn Hedge damage applies immediately if driven through thorn.

items.name: Antler Sweep
items.rider: A target standing in thicket is knocked Prone on a hit.

handler.note: Antler Sweep hit — if the target stands in thicket, it is knocked Prone.

events.description: GM cue when Antler Sweep deals damage.

items.name: It Defends, It Does Not Hunt
items.text: GM-run: bloodied (≤ half HP), a healthy fellstag walls itself off behind risen thorn and departs — it wanted you out, not dead. (The blight-gray variant never leaves.)

Sevenbrand Construct-Smith.biography:
A Builder-devout master smith of Brandmere (canon §5c/§9, rulings 77/80) — Red/White, quiet Kethane minority, Civilization-tree talents run AS WRITTEN (rulings 40/49; Investiture 4 covers forge + siege + one re-forge; the construct's stats come off talent-summons.json scaled to the smith). Deflect 3 = smith's leathers and mail. The tell in play: a 'procurement clerk's escort' whose bodyguard is forged metal announces whose devout builds the Warlock's war-machine.

Scaling: smith + construct is the rival unit — the construct is the frontline, the smith repairs and re-forges from behind Siege Form fire.

items.name: Reads the Marks
items.text: Flavor: names any forge-town's work on sight; own brands ladder the forearm — Builder-devout, Sevenbrand-proven, and a PC who knows the credential culture reads exactly that.

items.name: Behind the Work
items.text: GM-run: the construct is the frontline; the smith re-forges it if it falls and fights from behind Siege Form fire. Bloodied (≤ half HP), the smith yields — the work is proven; the smith need not die for it. A captured Builder-devout smith talks about Brandmere reluctantly, but honestly.

handler.note: Bloodied — the smith yields; the work is proven, the smith need not die for it.

events.description: GM morale cue at half HP.

The Garden Sow.biography:
The Warden (canon §5c, ruling 97) — the capital garden country's pair-attuned apex (Blue/Green, ruling 69), nexus-fed (ruling 89): a boar sow of impossible size and age, never sick, wounds closing like the healers' work. She keeps every other predator out of the district, and the folk keep the old agreement — the first furrow's crop at the field edge, no hunting inside the charter-stones. Spi 13 = the nexus's density in her.

The countdown variant (ruling 88, GM-timed): when the front bites the nexus she sickens first — same block, LOSES Nexus-Fed, hp 45, never tougher (ruling 34). The session she takes a wound that doesn't close, the countdown has arrived on screen.

items.name: Trampling Charge
items.rider: She moves up to her speed in a straight line first; on a hit the target is knocked Prone.

handler.note: Trampling Charge hit — the target is knocked Prone.

events.description: GM cue when the charge's damage lands (edha-on-hit carries it).

items.name: Nexus-Fed
items.text: The ground will not let her fail: at the end of each of her turns she regains 5 HP — engine-applied (never while she is down, never past max), with a whispered GM card.

handler.note: Nexus-Fed — the Sow regains 5 HP.

events.description: Engine-applied turn-end regen (edha-regen, ruling 98 — the handler's first consumer).

items.name: Rooted Fury
items.text: The first time she drops below half HP in a scene, the gardens' patience ends: Trampling Charge costs 1 Action for the rest of the scene.

handler.note: Rooted Fury — Trampling Charge now costs 1 Action for the rest of the scene.

events.description: GM cue on the drop below half.

items.name: The Old Agreement
items.text: She ignores any creature standing still and bearing no drawn steel inside the charter-stones — and never forgets a creature that broke the agreement. NO NAMEABLE HOOK: NPC intent/targeting isn't data (the Pack Tactics class); the GM plays the agreement.

Keelshadow.biography:
The Toll-Taker (canon §5c, ruling 97) — the clean grounds' pelagic rival (ruling 90): it paces hulls from below, takes the catch off the long-lines, and once in a bad year takes the man hauling them. Movement 60 = swim; it cannot leave the water — beached it is a salvage job, not a fight. Keelshadow sign is good fishing; the boats pay it off the ledger (first fish of every set over the side, uncounted).

Encounter frame: it fights from beneath — the deck is cover, the rail is the front line, and anything that goes in the water changes sides of the map.

items.name: Hull-Shadow
items.text: It strikes from under the hull — the shadow on the water is the only warning. On its first attack against each target per scene, the target tests Perception (with advantage — the shadow is legible) against its Cognitive defense; Breach and Drag's +1d6 rider applies against the fooled.

handler.note: Breach and Drag's +1d6 rider applies vs the fooled.

events.description: Engine-rolled belief test on its first attack per target per scene (ambush-belief ledger; whenTargetFooled riders read it).

items.name: Breach and Drag
items.rider: +1d6 against a character taken in by the hull-shadow. A hit target at a rail or in the water is dragged in/under (DC 13 Athletics to catch hold).

events.description: +1d6 when the current target is taken in by Hull-Shadow.

handler.note: Breach and Drag hit — if the target is at a rail or in the water, it is dragged in/under (DC 13 Athletics to catch hold).

events.description: GM cue when the bite's damage lands — the drag is a table read (positioning).

items.name: Sounding Dive
items.text: When it takes damage, it sounds: it dives deep and cannot be targeted from the surface until it breaches again at the start of its next turn.

handler.note: Sounding Dive — it dives: untargetable from the surface until it breaches at the start of its next turn.

events.description: GM cue whenever it takes damage.

items.name: Pay the Ledger
items.text: A boat that gives the first of its catch over the side is not molested that set — it takes the toll and drops back into the dark. NO NAMEABLE HOOK: NPC intent/targeting isn't data; the GM plays the toll.

Cinderbrock.biography:
The Wrack-Burner (canon §5c, ruling 97) — the Red spur's beast (ruling 35): badger-sized, furnace-hot, striped like burnt grass. Hills in summer, beaches in winter; the north coast's dawn smoke is cinderbrocks firing wrack over the mussel beds to pop them open. Deflect 2 = dense hide and heat-shimmer. Placid until denned or interrupted mid-fire — then explosive. It digs (burrower; dens in dry banks and steaming slag tips).

The Vorsk carters won't kill one — you don't kick the hearth. Encounter frame: usually a hazard negotiation, not a hunt; it defends its fire and its den.

items.name: Furnace Heart
items.text: Its body is forge-hot: any creature that starts its turn adjacent (within 5 ft) takes 1 energy damage. Grappling it unprotected is a bad idea the first second.

handler.note: Furnace Heart — 1 energy to any hostile starting its turn within 5 ft.

events.description: GM cue at each adjacent hostile's turn start.

items.name: Fire the Wrack
items.text:
Pyre, adapted (ruling 98) — the engine runs Fire the Wrack on Pyre's hazard path: edha-place-hazard region + the Pyre spread watcher by alias.

It sparks a prepared wrack-pile or dry cover within reach: a 10-ft square becomes burning ground (dangerous terrain) for the scene — 1d6 energy on entering or starting a turn inside, auto-dealt by the region. At the end of each of its turns the fire spreads to one adjacent flammable square (GM-judged, via the spread card).

events.description: Pyre's engine path: place a 10-ft burning Region (auto-damages on enter / turn start); the Pyre spread watcher runs it via EDHA_PYRE_SOURCES.

items.name: Den Fury
items.text: The first time it drops below half HP in a scene it burns hotter as it panics: Ember Bite deals +1d4 energy for the rest of the scene.

handler.note: Den Fury — Ember Bite deals +1d4 energy for the rest of the scene.

events.description: GM cue on the drop below half.

Cold-Fire Cinderbrock.biography:
The cold fire (canon §5c, rulings 97/90/34) — a cinderbrock that ate the thin catch off blighted beds and took the stuck-wasting: still burning, no longer living. Weaker, wrong, pitiable — steel works (ruling 34: the wasting never makes a creature tougher). It builds no fires now and defends nothing; it simply does not stop, and does not die of what it has. The north-beach folk give one a wide berth and, sometimes, a mercy.

Loses Fire the Wrack and Den Fury (it builds nothing and the panic burned out); Furnace Heart persists — wrongly, horribly, on a body that is mostly gone.

items.name: Furnace Heart
items.text: The heat has not understood: any creature that starts its turn adjacent (within 5 ft) takes 1 energy damage.

handler.note: Furnace Heart — 1 energy to any hostile starting its turn within 5 ft.

events.description: GM cue at each adjacent hostile's turn start.

Callthief.biography:
The rim plains' White predator (canon §5c, ruling 106) — pattern reproduction: it learns a herd's call-line and sings it back a hair flat. Callthieves hunt in couples: one sings, one takes. The encounter is an influence duel over the herd, not a stat slug — the herder sings the true line, the callthief counter-sings, and the beasts follow whichever voice carries. Kit is the White tree's own, names verbatim so the engine automation rides: Guiding Signal / Counterpoint / Overwhelming Authority.

Scaling: a couple (count 2) is one rival-weight encounter; add a second couple, never a lone singer — the kit assumes the pair.

items.name: Sing the Borrowed Line
items.text:
The borrowed call — a learned line, a hair flat.

It performs a call-line it has learned. Make an influence test (its Deception 4) against each beast or mount within 60 ft that knows the line, resolved through the normal influence rules; an influenced animal spends its next turn moving toward the callthief. Overwhelming Authority (below, engine name-keyed) rides each success: the influenced beast is also Disoriented until the end of the callthief's next turn. Stock that is sung-with at dusk (the custom, canon §5b) and trained war-mounts test with an advantage. While its borrowed line holds an animal, that animal counts as the callthief's ally for Counterpoint.

items.name: Guiding Signal
items.text:
White talent, name verbatim (engine name-keyed; Stitchmother/Reknit Form precedent).

Spend 1 Focus to designate a character or beast within 60 ft — the singer marks the one to take. The next test its partner makes against the marked target raises the stakes.

items.name: Counterpoint
items.text:
White talent, name verbatim (engine name-keyed).

When a character within 60 ft successfully influences a beast the callthief's borrowed line holds (sings the true line), it counter-sings: test White (its Deception). On a success, spend 1 Focus to negate the effect and Disorient the singer until the end of its next turn. This is the duel's core beat — voice against voice, through the contest core.

items.name: Overwhelming Authority
items.text:
White talent, name verbatim (engine name-keyed).

When it successfully influences a character or beast, spend 1 Focus: the target is also Disoriented until the end of its next turn — what answers the flat note stumbles out of the herd.

items.name: Take the Answerer
items.rider: +1d4 keen against a Disoriented target — the stumbler is the meal.

handler.note: If the target is Disoriented, add +1d4 keen to the damage — the answerer taken mid-stumble.

events.description: GM cue when Take the Answerer lands — the Disoriented rider is a table read (status check), cue is the floor.

items.name: Hunts in Couples
items.text: GM-run pack shape, no trigger: one sings from cover while the other circles. If the singer is silenced or dropped, the taker breaks off — the kit assumes the pair, and a lone callthief will not press a fight.

The False Spring.biography:
The Hush's apex (canon §5c, ruling 106) — pair-attuned Red/Blue on Ashkar's ruled ground (ruling 35 bleeding east). Almost never seen as itself: its trick is the held mirage — a believable oasis kept steady for hours at the exact distance a dying traveler will walk. The Blue is the illusion pair (Holographic Illusion + Living Image, engine name-keyed); the Red is the flats themselves (Kindle's glare, Afterburn's heat). Caravan law: unsung water is no water.

Scaling: one, ever — it is a set-piece and an omen, not a wandering monster. Pairs with the heat and the open white, never with adds.

items.name: The Held Oasis
items.text:
Blue adaptation: Holographic Illusion + Living Image (engine name-keyed pair) worn as a place — a scene-long oasis, fronds moving, water glinting, true parallax.

Anyone approaching the spring it has built tests Perception against its Cognitive defense (engine-rolled): on a failure the oasis is real to them until they touch it. Its first strike against each fooled target is made from the mirage.

handler.note: Glare-Strike's +1d6 rider applies vs the fooled — the drink that was not there.

events.description: Engine-rolled belief test on its first attack against each target per scene — the strike out of the mirage (ambush-belief ledger; whenTargetFooled riders read it).

items.name: Glare-Strike
items.rider: +1d6 against a character who is taken in by the mirage.

events.description: +1d6 (flavor-labeled on the roll) when the current target is taken in by The Held Oasis.

items.name: Kindle
items.text:
Red talent, name verbatim (engine name-keyed).

Its energy damage deals +1 additional damage (the Red-modifier term, resolved by ruling 107: leyline rank ≡ tier). Creatures it deals energy damage to shed light in 5 ft and lose concealment benefits until the end of its next turn — on the white flats, what the glare has touched cannot hide from it.

handler.note: Kindle: +1 energy (Red modifier ≡ tier, ruling 107); light/concealment half is the name-keyed engine path.

events.description: Carries Kindle's damage-rider shape verbatim; the Red-modifier bonus resolves to +tier (ruling 107).

items.name: Afterburn
items.text:
Red talent, name verbatim (engine name-keyed). Opportunity is trusted — never auto-deducted.

When it deals energy damage, it may spend an Opportunity to leave the target Afflicted [half 1d4 energy] — heatstroke riding the wound.

handler.note: Red/Conflagration. After it deals energy damage, spend an Opportunity to leave the target Afflicted [half 1d4 energy] ongoing — heatstroke. Opportunity is trusted (no auto-deduct). Target the creature, then accept the prompt.

events.description: Carries the PC Afterburn rule verbatim; [Tier][Die] resolved by ruling 107 (leyline rank ≡ tier): tier 1 → 1d4.

items.name: Heat of the Flats
items.text: Characters who start their turn within 10 ft of it in open glare lose 1 focus — the pan's heat is its second weapon.

handler.note: This character loses 1 focus (open glare; shade or full cover negates — table read).

events.description: GM cue when a hostile starts its turn within 10 ft — the heat pressure (Furnace Heart shape).

items.name: Gone Into the Shimmer
items.text: GM-run: bloodied (≤ half HP), it drops the oasis mid-scene — the water simply is not there anymore — and walks into its own heat-haze, gone. It does not fight to the death; the pan does the rest.

handler.note: It drops the mirage and disengages into the heat-haze — end of the fight, start of the walk home.

events.description: GM cue at half HP — the withdrawal (Patient-Not-Cruel shape).

Dirgehound Pack.biography:
Pan-edge canids of the Altar-corner Black (canon §5c, ruling 106) — they attend the given herds: locked stock emit nothing to a death-sense, so the packs trail what the law gave to the Hush and wait for what still kills mechanically (ruling 9). Folk hear the night-song as the Hush reading its ledger. The Black tree's isolation cluster on four legs — kit names verbatim so the engine automation rides (incl. the Dread Presence movement veto, its first bestiary reuse).

Scaling: three hounds are one rival-weight encounter — add hounds, never hp. They cut one out; they do not swarm the line.

items.name: Dread Presence
items.text:
Black talent, name verbatim — the engine's preUpdateToken veto rides the name.

Weakened characters within 30 ft cannot willingly move closer to any allies — the pack's song stands between the straggler and the line.

items.name: Unnerving Approach
items.text:
Black talent, name verbatim (engine name-keyed).

Once per turn, when it moves adjacent to an enemy, spend 1 Focus: choose one character allied to that enemy within 10 ft and push them 5 ft directly away — the shoulder that cuts the straggler out, potentially leaving the target Isolated.

items.name: Predatory Patience
items.text:
Black talent, name verbatim (engine name-keyed).

When it attacks a Weakened creature, add 1d4 to the test; on a successful attack against a Weakened creature it regains 1 Focus — it has waited days already.

events.description: Carries the PC Predatory Patience test rider verbatim; 1d4 = 1d(2·rank+2) at leyline rank ≡ tier 1 (ruling 107). Target the creature first.

handler.note: If the target is Weakened: the dirgehound regains 1 Focus (GM adds — adversary focus has no auto-write).

events.description: GM cue on a landed hit — the Focus regain half of Predatory Patience, cue as the floor.

items.name: Predator's Due
items.text:
Black talent — carries the PC talent's authored rule shape verbatim (Sudden Wall precedent).

When it reduces a character to 0 health, it regains 1d4 health and 1 Focus — and feeds.

handler.note: Predator's Due: +1d4 health ([Tier][Die] at rank ≡ tier 1, ruling 107) and 1 Focus on the kill (focus is a GM add).

events.description: Black/Ritual. On reducing a character to 0 HP: regain 1d4 health (engine-applied; ruling 107 dice) + 1 Focus (GM adds).

items.name: Worry the Straggler
items.rider: +1d4 keen against an Isolated or Weakened target — the cut-out one.

handler.note: If the target is Isolated or Weakened, add +1d4 keen — the pack takes the cut-out one.

events.description: GM cue when Worry the Straggler lands — the Isolated/Weakened rider is a table read, cue is the floor.

items.name: They Attend the Given Herds
items.text: GM-run encounter seed, no trigger: a dirgehound pack near the pan edge is following something — usually a given herd, sometimes a caravan that smells of the failing. Their presence is information: the Hush's ledger has an open entry nearby.
